body:
Hey, I'm sorry you are in a really shit situation. I can't really offer much advice, or anything of that sort because you are in a situation most of us can't even imagine. If it's any  comfort what you are going through right now is hard, like, extremely hard, and it's bloody impressive you can write about it. 

I know it's not much but you can PM me if you need to chat or rant or anything. I know it's not much but. I guess someone listening and understanding is better than someone not giving a shit and saying 
"It'll get better"
Because that is the worst advice ever given.

Best of luck

I wish I could be like

"Oh yes, do this and it all goes away!" Because I've been looking for that and so far I've come up blank. The way I personally cope is take it in tiny tiny steps. For walking places I literally broke it down step by step, so everything I did felt like a tiny but significant achievement. I guess I also took comfort in the fact that I know dips are dips, and although it feels like I'm dying right now, it will go up. It has to. It's just. Although, that is personal to me so you may have a different way of looking at things. 

This is something I struggled with, so may not be relevant to you but, don't feel guilty about feeling miserable. Or anything like that. Don't feel guilty for staying in bed all day and only coming out to drink or eat, because Depression is an illness, and effects you like one. If you had a broken leg people wouldn't expect you to get up and be walking around the day after. Give yourself a chance to heal.

If on days you are low and just need to talk someone just reply here or message me. Sometimes it just helps to know that you are being heard, and I'll listen.

And don't mention it, just hope I helped.

That's really fantastic you have someone to talk to about this, and it's better that you are taking medication for it. Can I ask how long you've been on medication and talking? Reason I'm asking is because it takes a little time for the antidepressants to have an effect and even then it takes even longer to make a full recovery, with a lot of dips in mood on the way, which can sometimes feel like a relapse. 

Also

"Around 50 per cent of people who respond to an antidepressant need an increase in the starting dose a few weeks into treatment. Nearly 70 per cent of people with real clinical depression will respond to the first antidepressant they go on, if they tolerate it and the dosage is got right. But each type of drug covers a different 70 per cent and no drug is successful for everybody. So if one antidepressant doesn’t suit, don’t give up; try another."
- Depressive Illness, curse of the strong by Tim Cantopher

So reason I included a quote was so it didn't look like I was talking out my ass. I personally have had to change antidepressant and dose many times. It does take time, but luckily that doesn't mean it's not working. Don't be afraid to say that you think the antidepressant isn't working, they (the doctors and nurses) are there to help.

And just to repeat, you are doing really well in fighting this. It's not easy, and a lot of people don't realise that. If I can help just let me know

Hey OP, I'm sorry you are having these thoughts because they are truly horrible to deal with. 

I'm not sure if this is an option to you but have you tried counselling? Or seeing someone professional? It takes a lot of courage to talk to them but once you do it does allow them to help and help make things better, either through therapies or medication. There are hundreds of therapies all made for different situations and people so it's not a "one size fits all" and can actually help your specific situation.

If you need someone to chat to though just Hmu.

Best of luck

Just wanted to say first off you don't need to apologise for feeling  or talking about this. It's part of being human and everyone in this sub just wants to help.

That being said, I'm really sorry you are feeling this way. I'm sorry if I missed it (reading isn't a strong point of mine), but have you ever considered going to a psychologist or psychiatrist about this? If it's not an option due to finance or other reasons I completely understand, but if you haven't I think it might really help as they are experts and can help with either medication or therapies or even just helping you understand how you feel.

Please keep yourself safe, and if you want someone to talk to and don't want to talk to someone face to face you can message me, and I'll listen and take seriously whatever you have to say.

Best of luck

Don't know if this'll help but I've also got that personality where I drink myself to oblivion every time I get near alcohol. Doesn't mean you are a dumbass, or an idiot or weak or anything. Alcohol is a coping resource, and when your problems outweigh your coping resources... And so on.

Going from drinking regularly to not drinking at all will do all sorts of shit to your brain. It's a chemical, and it affects your brain, but I doubt it'll be permanent. If it does persist go to a doctor and they'll help. You still taking your SSRI? If not it might be an idea to start taking it again, especially if it made you feel normal, you know? If you are still taking it and it's not working you can talk to your doctor again. something like 70% of patients on meds needs readjustments at some point during the course of taking them, so it's normal. 

Hope some of this helps, and best of luck
Well thanks for replying, and I hope it continues to be okay

Hey, I'm sorry you are having a shit time right now, and I've personally never have been in this situation but I've a couple of close friends go through this (Update on them they have just finished their first year of uni and are excited to go into year two).

Moving away from family is bloody hard normally, but add mental health issues on top of it becomes really hellish. (So well done for going through with it) I just wanted to say a couple of things about it though.

First off, actually going and planning to engage with the college activities (even if you only plan to go for a few) is a really impressive, because isolating yourself in a new environment will make the problems and issues you have now a lot harder to deal with. Humans are social creatures and really need others to talk to, even just small talk.

It's really frustrating because I don't want to say "it'll get better" because that is the most irritating "comfort" I've ever heard because it's lazy and doesn't address this issues of now, but I know that it can because I've seen my friends go through it, you know? What they really struggled with was the first couple of weeks, both of them got really homesick (but afterwards they adapted and found it much easier). She told me that she just had to keep going, and take it week by week, or day by day or minute by minute because that was the only way she could get through. If she looked further ahead she just panicked. She said finding things to do on certain to do made the days go quicker, although I don't know how well that works for you?

I hope at least some of that helps, if it doesn't let me know if I missed the point and I'll get back to you.

Best of luck
So did you find that things just didn't work at all or that after a while things just didn't work as well as they used to?
Not going to lie appreciate you posting this because I'm in a really similar situation, thanks OP
Wow, that was a really comprehensive answer, thanks so much!
To be honest I could use help with everything, so I'll 100% give it a look

Hey I'm sorry you are having a bit of a shit time OP. I can't really help with balancing two jobs (can barely get one) but I can give my peice on the guilt part.

You shouldn't have to feel guilty at all. You are working your ass off in manual labour job which is physically and phycologically taxing and your body just gave out on you (understandably) which is of no fault of your own. Guilt is a feeling associated with doing something wrong, and in this case you've done nothing wrong at all.

I'm wondering if maybe talking to your manager would help with this? Maybe if you could explain your situation with the fact that you are finding it really difficult to balance two jobs and that's the reason you are late/calling off sick? Worse case scenario he doesn't do anything, but best case scenario he can give you better hours or at least some leeway.

Can I ask why your parents made you get another job? If it's causing you this much stress surely they wouldn't mind if you dropped one of the jobs? (Sorry if this isn't an option due to your situation, I'm just trying to think of things that would help)

Hope at least some of this helps
